messages.subject: הערכת מודל בעזרת רגרסיה לוגיסטית
parts:
היי,
יש לי קובץ נתונים גדול שמכיל מספר רק של עמודות
חילקתי את הקובץ הגדול ל 70% אימון ו 30% בדיקה
ds_tr
ds_te

המטרה שלי זה להעריך את אחת העמודות ששמה 
popularity
והיא משתנה מסוג פאקטור עם שתי אפשרויות:
High \ Low
ולהתעלם מעמודה ששמה 
url

בניתי את המודל הבא:
mdl <- glm(formula = popularity ~ . -url , family= "binomial", data = ds_tr )

לאחר מכן עשיתי את הדבר הבא בשביל לקבל ריקול ופריסיון על נתוני האימון

y_hat = predict(mdl, data = ds_tr - url , type = 'response')
y = (ds_tr$popularity == "High")
x= y_hat > 0.5
tp = sum(((x==TRUE) & (y==TRUE)))   # true positive
tn = sum(((x==!TRUE) & (y==!TRUE)))   # true negative
fp = sum(((x==!TRUE) & (y==TRUE)))   # true negative
fn = sum(((x==TRUE) & (y==!TRUE)))   # true negative
results$In_Sample_Err[1]= tp/(tp+fp)#precision
results$In_Sample_Err[2]= tp/(tp+fn) # recall

לאחר מכן אני מנסה לעשות אותו דבר על נתוני הבדיקה אך נתקלת בבעיה
> y_hat = predict(mdl, data = ds_te - url , type = 'response')
> y = (ds_te$popularity == "High")
> x= y_hat > 0.5
> tp = sum(((x==TRUE) & (y==TRUE)))   # true positive
Warning message:
In (x == TRUE) & (y == TRUE) :
  longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length
> tn = sum(((x==!TRUE) & (y==!TRUE)))   # true negative
Warning message:
In (x == (!TRUE)) & (y == (!TRUE)) :
  longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length
> fp = sum(((x==!TRUE) & (y==TRUE)))   # true negative
Warning message:
In (x == (!TRUE)) & (y == TRUE) :
  longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length
> fn = sum(((x==TRUE) & (y==!TRUE)))   # true negative
Warning message:
In (x == TRUE) & (y == (!TRUE)) :
  longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length
> results$In_Sample_Out[1]= tp/(tp+fp)#precision
> results$In_Sample_Out[1]= tp/(tp+fn) # recall


הבעיה נוצרת כי הגדלים לא מתאימים, רציתי לעשות את השורה הבאה במקום:
 y_hat = predict(mdl, newdata =ds_te - url , type = 'response')
Error in FUN(left, right) : non-numeric argument to binary operator
In addition: Warning message:
In Ops.factor(left, right) : ‘-’ not meaningful for factors

בנוסף ניסיתי גם

 y_hat = predict(mdl, newdata =ds_te , type = 'response')
Error in model.frame.default(Terms, newdata, na.action = na.action, xlev = object$xlevels) : 
  factor url has new levels http://mashable.com/2013/01/07/apple-40-billion-app-downloads/, http://mashable.com/2013/01/07/canon-poweshot-n/, http://mashable.com/2013/01/07/dad-jokes/, http://mashable.com/2013/01/07/htc-q1/, http://mashable.com/2013/01/07/isp02-iphone-take-your-pulse/, http://mashable.com/2013/01/07/lego-taking-robotics-to-next-level-with-mindstorms-ev3/, http://mashable.com/2013/01/07/lionel-messi-fashion-moments/, http://mashable.com/2013/01/07/living-room-pinterest-contest/, http://mashable.com/2013/01/07/omron-fitness-monitors/, http://mashable.com/2013/01/07/polaroid-android-camera/, http://mashable.com/2013/01/07/rage-comics-dying/, http://mashable.com/2013/01/07/samsung-uhd-blu-ray/, http://mashable.com/2013/01/07/sharp-intros-worlds-largest-led-hdtv/, http://mashable.com/2013/01/07/sony-stops-manufacturing-playstation-2/, http://mashable.com/2013/01/07/stolen-iphone-dating/, http://mashable.com/2013/01/07/targus-touch-pen-windows-8/, http://mashable.com

messages.subject: Re: הערכת מודל בעזרת רגרסיה לוגיסטית
parts:
תנסי את זה אולי. תגידי מה יצא לך.

library("randomForest") # load the randomForest package
mdl= randomForest(popularity ~ . -url, data=ds_tr, ntree=100)
str(mdl)

library("ROCR")     
y_hat = predict(mdl, ds_tr, type="prob")
x = y_hat[,1] > 0.5
y = (ds_tr$popularity == "High")
tp = sum(((x==TRUE) & (y==TRUE)))
tn = sum(((x==!TRUE) & (y==!TRUE)))
fn = sum(((x==TRUE) & (y==!TRUE)))
results$In_Sample_Err[1]= tp/(tp+fp)#precision
fp = sum(((x==!TRUE) & (y==TRUE)))
results$In_Sample_Err[2]= tp/(tp+fn) # recall

y_hat = predict(mdl, ds_te, type="prob")
x = y_hat[,1] > 0.5
y = (ds_te$popularity == "High")
tp = sum(((x==TRUE) & (y==TRUE)))
tn = sum(((x==!TRUE) & (y==!TRUE)))
fn = sum(((x==TRUE) & (y==!TRUE)))
results$Out.of.Sample.Err[1]= tp/(tp+fp)#precision
fp = sum(((x==!TRUE) & (y==TRUE)))

results$Out.of.Sample.Err[2]= tp/(tp+fn) # recall

parts:
Hi,
Once you define a formula while training, you don't need to specify which columns are used in the test set. I changed your dataset to iris in order to check:

#Train
mdl <- glm(formula = Species ~ . -Petal.Width , family= "binomial", data = ds_tr )

#Test
y_hat = predict(mdl,ds_te,type = "response") #If you do want to specify the columns, use ds_te[,-5] or some other type of column subsetting.
y = (ds_te$Species == "virginica")

x= y_hat > 0.5
tp = sum(((x==TRUE) & (y==TRUE)))   # true positive
tn = sum(((x==!TRUE) & (y==!TRUE)))   # true negative
fp = sum(((x==!TRUE) & (y==TRUE)))   # true negative
fn = sum(((x==TRUE) & (y==!TRUE)))   # true negative

results$In_Sample_Out[1]= tp/(tp+fp)#precision
results$In_Sample_Out[2]= tp/(tp+fn) # recall #you had a wrong index here. it was [1] instead of [2]

It now works and the lengths of y and x are identical.

Regarding your other error (factor url has new levels), you could coerce it to character:
dataset$url <- as.character(dataset$url)
and then run the analysis.

If all that doesn't help, then it's a problem with your initial data. please post its structure + the code that you use for splitting to train and test.

Hope it helps!
